main_text.p: uro fancienda[?], modò sint poffibilia, jus-ta & honesta, Quinto, si aliquod statutum post juramentum præstitum abrogatum fuerit, vel in desuetudinem abeat; obligatio Juramenti quoad illud statutum cessat, ita ut non teneatur illud ultrà observare: nisi juratum fuerit verbis specialibus in ipsam rem statuto deretam; in eo enim casu sublato statuto manet tamen obligatio. Sexto, cum statuta Communitatum fere plurima sint, & multa multis ignota; & difficillimum fit, imò vix possibile omnia & singula exacto & examussim observare: ut bona fide ita se comparaverit, ut nihil quod est officii sui lubens prætereat, debitamque adhibuerit moralem diligentiam, ut ea omnia sciret quæ ad ipsius officium pertinent; statuerintque statui, honori, paci suæ Communitatis, quantum humana patitur infirmitas, fideliter & sine scandalo infervire; hunc ego non dubitarem fidem de statutis observandis à se datam bona conscientia actenus liberasse, & debitum ad quod obligavit, æqui boni lege exsolvisse. Quod item & de publicis Regni legibus intelligendum est.

page.notes: The scan cuts off the left edge of the text block, so the first letters of several lines are missing; the words there were completed from the context and marked [?] only where still doubtful (first word "fancienda"). The page number is printed in old style and read as 91 with doubt. The line-end hyphens "jus-", "prætterie-" and "ni-" are printed. The first letters of "sta-tutum", "Sexto", and "Quinto" are underlined or italic in the print, shown here as italic. Several long s characters are plain s as required; "est" is written as printed.
